latest_release.name: v0.15.0
latest_release.body:
Omnigraph 0.15 has five main highlights. Loading a large dataset into a new graph takes less than half the time it took in 0.14. Reads no longer wait for writes to commit. Most branch diffs and merges cost what changed, not how big the tables are or how long the history is. MCP agents get every graph operation, and your Cedar policy alone decides what each agent may run. S3 clusters close three ways in which two servers could write at once.

This release changes what MCP agents may call, how `@card` minimums and `@unique` are checked, managed organization commands, saved plans and a Rust error type. Read the upgrade actions before you upgrade. If you serve MCP, agents gain every tool that their policy allows, even if you never set an MCP flag. Graph storage does not change, and existing graphs open without a rebuild.

This page says what each change means for you. The [complete changelog](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/blob/v0.15.0/docs/releases/v0.15.0.md) keeps the change notes as they were published.

## Highlights

### CSV bulk load: a new graph in under half the 0.14 time

An initial import, or a rebuild from an export, now finishes in less than half the time. In local runs of the LDBC SNB SF30 dataset (34 GB of CSV, 31 load statements into a new graph, release builds on an Apple silicon workstation with local disk), the load took 261 seconds on 0.14.0 and 87 to 110 seconds on 0.15. Loads from S3 were not measured. An overwrite `load csv` now works as a pipeline: each parse thread reads its own 8 MiB pieces of the source, checks keys and edge endpoints as rows arrive, and writes data files while the next rows parse. Checks that a new graph cannot fail are skipped, and a refused load still leaves nothing behind. `append` and `merge` loads still read the whole source before they parse it. #1141, #1147, #1158, #1178

### Reads no longer wait for writes

Within one server process, a read that arrived while a write was committing used to wait for the commit, because the commit held a lock across a storage round trip; on S3 that is a network request. In 0.15 a read never waits for a write in the same process. A write that touches several tables, such as a node type and its edges, also commits them in parallel: two round trips at commit, where it took two for each table, so the next write on the branch starts sooner. The first read after another process commits sends 11 or 12 storage requests instead of 18 to 20. How it works: the graph's current state is an immutable value behind an atomic pointer, and a write swaps the pointer in one step. #1228, #1270, #1230

### Merges after 1,024 commits: 54 storage requests instead of 4,168

Reviewing or merging a branch used to cost more the larger the table and the longer its history: a diff read every row of each changed type, and a merge read every data file of each table. Now both read only what changed. Diffing ten updated rows in a type with 100,000 rows took 277 requests and 6.9 MB; it now takes 14 requests and 27 KB, the same as with 4,000 rows. After 1,024 one-row commits, a fast-forward merge sends 54 requests instead of 4,168, and a three-way merge 135 instead of 3,216. These counts come from Omnigraph's simulated in-memory store; on S3 each request is a network round trip. Lance keeps a stable ID for each row and the version that last wrote it, so Omnigraph reads only the rows whose version differs. A diff between two branches that have both moved, and a merge of a table with Blob properties, still compare everything. #1201, #1229,
#1301

### MCP: every graph operation, decided by your policy

An agent connected over MCP can now review a branch diff, find a merge base, publish or drop a proposed commit, and run a stored mutation; in 0.14 it needed HTTP for all of these. Only byte streams (Blob payloads and exports) stay HTTP and CLI only. Each tool runs its HTTP route's code under the same Cedar action, so an agent gets the same answers and refusals as an HTTP client

hot_issues.title: Attribute the served read floor (~0.2 s server-side on a trivial read) and expose it as usage
storage: safely reclaim obsolete physical __manifest versions and files
performance: merges into independent targets serialize behind graph-wide guards
server: async job API for /branches/merge — 202 + job_id, request-key idempotency
bug: retained branch reads use the original path after whole-root relocation (0.14.0)
Vector ANN is effectively brute-force: indexes are built with 1 IVF partition, and nearest() sets no probe budget
omnigraph-server: runtime reload of the bearer-token source (SIGHUP or admin endpoint)

detail.readme:
Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology.
Unified retrieval engine (vector/BM25/graph) · Git-style workflows · Open data format (Lance)

Quickstart  ·  Docs  ·  Cookbooks  ·  CLI  ·  Studio  ·  llms.txt

Omnigraph is engineered for the new workload introduced by long-horizon agents: multiple agents sharing a typed world model to continuously retrieve and update context and coordinate work. Agents and UIs can become thin stateless consumers of durable state. Omnigraph Cloud is in private preview: [join the waitlist](https://www.omnigraph.dev/cloud?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud-waitlist). Join the [Omnigraph Slack community](https://join.slack.com/t/omnigraphworkspace/shared_invite/zt-3wfpglyxj-lHvJGhuySPfqLtN35uJZNw) to ask questions, share feedback, and follow development. ## Capabilities | Capability | What it gives you | |---|---| | **Typed ontology** | Agents share one enforceable model of the domain. `.pg` schemas declare node and edge types, keys and constraints, and the engine enforces them on every write. | | **Multimodal retrieval** | Agents assemble high-precision & recall context in one query: graph traversal + vector ANN + full-text + Reciprocal Rank Fusion in **one** runtime, with filtering. | | **Branching** | Agents propose reviewable changes instead of writing to main: a branch per agent or task, three-way merge, time travel across the whole graph. | | **Declared as code** | A `cluster.yaml` declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, embedding providers and policies. `cluster plan` previews, `cluster apply` converges, Terraform-style. | | **Security as code** | Cedar policy enforced **server-side on every mutation**, per graph or server-wide; bearer auth, server-resolved actors, audit tracking. | | **Object-storage native, open format** | Decoupled storage and compute. Store graphs on local disk or S3-compatible storage: RustFS / MinIO, AWS S3 / R2, or Azure preview. Graph data uses open, versioned [Lance](https://github.com/lance-format/lance), including Blob values. | ## What you can build | Use case | What it's for | |---|---| | **Company brain** | Org knowledge unified into one graph every agent can query | | **Agentic memory** | Durable, versioned memory: a branch per agent or per task, merged on review | | **Context graph** | Decision traces and codified tribal knowledge for retrieval | | **Dev graph** | Issues & dependency model that coding agents read and write | | **R&D / ML data layer** | Experiments and trials written into branches, versioned for training & eval | ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` This installs `omnigraph` (CLI) and `omnigraph-server` into `~/.local/bin` from published release binaries. Or with Homebrew: ```bash brew tap ModernRelay/tap brew install ModernRelay/tap/omnigraph ``` ## Studio [Omnigraph Studio](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) is the desktop app for your graphs. Browse each type as a table, follow relationships on a canvas, write queries with the compiler's errors as you type, and review what a branch changes before you merge it. It is a native Rust app on GPUI, the framework behind Zed, for macOS, Windows and Linux. Open a graph on one of your server targets in Studio: ```bash omnigraph studio --target --graph ``` [Download Studio](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) or read [its source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-studio). ## Set it up with an AI agent Omnigraph is built to be run by coding agents. Two ways in: **Teach your agent the playbook.** The `omnigraph` binary carries the [**`omnigraph` agent skill**](skills/omnigraph) written for it: the operational playbook covering cluster mode, the two config surfaces, schema evolution, query linting, data writes, branches, Cedar policy, and the common gotchas. Export it where your agent loads skills, so the skill always matches the installed CLI: ```bash omnigraph skill export ~/.claude/skills/omnigraph --force ``` With an older CLI that has no `skill` command, or none installed, `npx skills add ModernRelay/omnigraph@omnigraph` installs the copy on the default branch instead. **Or have an agent set it up from scratch.** Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, or any agent that can read a URL and run a shell command: ```text Read https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/blob/main/skills/omnigraph/references/onboarding.md and follow it to set up Omnigraph for me. ``` The agent installs the CLI, asks what the graph is for, builds and queries a small local graph, and then points to the cookbooks, a cluster or Omnigraph Cloud. For ready-to-run graphs with real seed data (company brain, VC operating system, pharma & industry intel), [`ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks`](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks) is the fastest way to see Omnigraph shaped to a real domain. ## Deploy A **cluster** declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, and policies in a configuration bundle. `cluster plan` previews changes and `cluster apply` submits them to the selected destination. The cluster-only HTTP server exposes graphs at `/graphs/{id}/…` and activates applied changes without a restart. Keep desired configuration separate from its destination: ``` company-brain/ ├── cluster.yaml ├── people.pg # schema for the "knowledge" graph ├── queries/ # stored queries: the .gq files ARE the declaration │ └── people.gq ├── cluster.policy.yaml # deployment permissions └── graph.policy.yaml # graph permissions ``` ```yaml # cluster.yaml version: 1 metadata: name: company-brain graphs: knowledge: schema: people.pg queries: queries/ # every `query ` in queries/*.gq registers policies: cluster-access: file: cluster.policy.yaml applies_to: [cluster] graph-access: file: graph.policy.yaml applies_to: [knowledge] ``` For first boot, follow the [cluster guide](docs/user/clusters/index.md#bootstrap-a-cluster), including writer ownership transfer and authentication. The [deployment guide](docs/user/deployment.md) covers containers and object stores; Azure writers require its admission wrapper. The applied cluster policy must grant the authenticated operator `config_manage`. Schema changes also require `read` and `schema_apply` on the affected graphs. With those grants and a server target named `production`, deploy local edits: ```bash omnigraph cluster validate --config ./company-brain omnigraph cluster plan --target production --config ./company-brain omnigraph cluster apply --target production --config ./company-brain ``` `--config` names the source bundle; `--target` names the destination. Omitting `storage` from the bundle uses the selected destination's root. If present, `storage` must match that root; it never selects or redirects the target. Apply prints a deployment ID. If delivery is interrupted, inspect that ID before submitting again; see [deployment recovery](docs/user/clusters/index.md). ## Query and mutate Define a server target with `default_graph` and set `defaults.target` once in `~/.omnigraph/config.yaml` ([configuration](docs/user/cli/index.md)), and the everyday commands stay short. Stored queries and mutations run **by name**: ```bash omnigraph query search_docs --params '{"q":"AI safety"}' omnigraph mutate add_person --params '{"name":"Mina"}' ``` Branch, review and merge across the whole graph, so agents write in isolation: ```bash omnigraph branch create --from main agent/ingest-42 omnigraph branch merge agent/ingest-42 --into main ``` An **alias** is shorter still: bind a target, graph, and stored query to one name, then `omnigraph alias triage` runs it. Data commands use `--target NAME` for a configured server or managed resource, plus `--graph ID` when needed. Use `--target ./graph.omni` for a standalone local graph. Control-plane login and organization operations use `--profile`; see [operator configuration](docs/user/cli/targets.md). ## Security & governance - **Engine-wide enforcement:** every write path goes through the same Cedar gate, so the HTTP server, the CLI, and the embedded SDK obey identical rules. - **Declared in the cluster:** a policy bundle is bound to graphs (or the whole server) via `policies:` → `applies_to`. - **Scoped:** rules apply per graph, per branch, or server-wide. - **Static server credentials:** static bearer tokens are hashed at startup and compared in constant time. - **Forge-proof identity:** the actor is resolved server-side from the token; clients can't set it. See the [policy guide](docs/user/operations/policy.md). ## Clients & SDKs | Client | Use it for | Where | |---|---|---| | **TypeScript SDK** | typed access from Node / TS | [`@modernrelay/omnigraph`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modernrelay/omnigraph) · [source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-ts) | | **Built-in MCP** | connect an agent to the server's `/mcp`, directly or through `omnigraph mcp --target NAME` | [MCP guide](docs/user/operations/mcp.md) | | **Omnigraph Studio** | browse, query and review a graph in a desktop app | [download](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) · [source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-studio) | | **HTTP / OpenAPI** | use the wire contract from any language | [HTTP guide](docs/user/operations/server.md) · [OpenAPI](openapi.json) | Match the client's HTTP contract to the server's. The 0.14 server requires contract `0.14`; see [client availability](docs/user/install.md#client-compatibility) before selecting an npm package. ## Docs - [0.14 highlights and upgrade actions](docs/releases/v0.14.0-overview.md) · [User guide](docs/user/index.md) - [Cluster guide](docs/user/clusters/index.md) · [Deployment guide](docs/user/deployment.md) · [CLI reference](docs/user/cli/reference.md) - [Schema](docs/user/schema/index.md) · [Queries](docs/user/queries/index.md) · [Search](docs/user/search/index.md) · [Policy](docs/user/operations/policy.md) ## Build and test ```bash cargo build --workspace --locked cargo test --workspace --exclude omnigraph-gqt --exclude omnigraph-gqt-served --exclude omnigraph-dst --locked \ --features omnigraph-engine/failpoints,omnigraph-cluster/failpoints ``` Notes: - Rust stable toolchain, edition 2024 - The GQT corpus (`cargo test -p omnigraph-gqt`) and the DST suite (`cargo test` from `crates/omnigraph-dst`, which supplies its process environment) run separately; a plain `cargo test --workspace` starts the DST binaries without that environment and they refuse. Commands and CI gates: [docs/dev/testing.md](docs/dev/testing.md) - Full CI and some local test flows require `protobuf-compiler` - S3 integration tests expect an S3-compatible endpoint such as RustFS ## Contributing Please open an issue before sending large code changes — a maintainer triages it, and the `accepted` label is the green light for a PR (see [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md)). Concrete problem statements are the fastest way to collaborate on the roadmap. ## Community Join the [Omnigraph Slack community](https://join.slack.com/t/omnigraphworkspace/shared_invite/zt-3wfpglyxj-lHvJGhuySPfqLtN35uJZNw) to ask questions, share feedback, and follow development.
